title: Mastering Animal Welfare Certification: Key Compliance Strategies for Success
text:
Colombia Advances Animal Welfare Standards with New Resolutions Colombia is taking significant steps to enhance animal welfare standards across various sectors, including cattle farming , animal exhibitions , and transportation. Several resolutions have been enacted to provide comprehensive guidelines and regulations, ensuring better treatment and management of animals. Thes initiatives reflect Colombia’s commitment to improving animal welfare practices and aligning with international standards. The resolutions address critical areas such as training for animal handlers, certification for livestock farms, and regulations for animal transport, all aimed at fostering a more humane and ethical environment for animals.
Key Resolutions and Guidelines María eugenia Buitrago, a Professional of Health programs in the Sub-Directorate of Animal Health and Welfare of Fedegán-FNG, has highlighted the most significant resolutions currently in effect. These resolutions cover a range of animal welfare aspects, from general conditions to specific requirements for different industries.
Animal welfare Conditions Manual The cornerstone of Colombia’s animal welfare framework is the Animal Welfare Conditions Manual , established by Resolution 253 issued in October 2020 . This manual provides detailed guidelines for the welfare of cattle, buffaline, corral birds, and aquatic animals. It serves as a benchmark for assessing and improving animal welfare conditions across these sectors.
Regulation of Zoocriaderos and Animal Exhibition Events Resolution 000366 of 2024 focuses on regulating animal welfare conditions in Zoocriaderos and animals concentration and exhibition events , including auctions, fairs, and sales sites. This resolution mandates that individuals involved in handling animals at these venues must undergo basic training in animal welfare and management.
According to buitrago, the Colombian Agricultural institute (ICA) is responsible for developing a Training plan for animal handlers and determining authorized certification bodies. The ICA will also establish a METHODOLOGY TO EVALUATE THE CONDITIONS of animal welfare at these sites, ensuring compliance with the standards outlined in the resolution.
The resolution emphasizes the importance of skilled and informed personnel in maintaining high animal welfare standards at events and facilities where animals are concentrated.
Certification in Animal Welfare for Primary Livestock Production Resolution 00016409 of 2024 outlines the requirements for certification in animal welfare for primary livestock production. This standard allows livestock owners to voluntarily certify their farms based on animal welfare conditions.
Buitrago explained that to obtain certification, livestock owners must request an evaluation of their facilities based on the conditions established in Resolution 253 of 2020. This voluntary certification programme aims to incentivize and recognize farms that adhere to high animal welfare standards.
Regulation of Animal Transport The Resolution Mintransport and ICA 20223040006915 of 2022 regulates animal transport in Colombia. This resolution sets standards for the safe and humane transportation of animals across the country.
Buitrago detailed that the resolution includes a transition period for compliance, with a deadline of 36 months as of December 20, 2024 . This means that training, evaluations, and implementation of the provisions must be completed before december 2027.
Colombia’s Achievements in Animal Welfare edilberto Sierra brito,Deputy Manager of Animal Protection of the ICA,highlighted the issuance of Resolution 16409 as a significant achievement in 2024. This resolution marks the first time that land is certified for complying with animal care principles.
In Armenia we launched with first properties and Today we have 38 properties in less than a month,and more than 200 applications
Edilberto Sierra brito,Deputy Manager of Animal Protection of the ICA
Sierra Brito also emphasized colombia’s role in hosting the first workshop on animal welfare organized in America by the World Organization for Animal Health (OMSA) in November of last year. He sees this as a “milestone” that solidifies Colombia’s regional and global leadership in animal welfare.
Maybe some like very high standards in well -being, perhaps others do not believe in those standards but we do sit down to talk, we reach some agreements in which the benefit in the end will be for the same animals, national production and food security of the country
Edilberto Sierra Brito, Deputy Manager of Animal Protection of the ICA
Conclusion Colombia’s commitment to animal welfare is evident through its comprehensive set of resolutions and initiatives. By establishing clear guidelines, providing training, and offering certification programs, Colombia is working to improve the lives of animals across various sectors. These efforts not only enhance animal welfare but also contribute to the sustainability and ethical practices within the country’s agricultural industry. The ongoing implementation and enforcement of these resolutions will be crucial in ensuring long-term improvements in animal welfare standards throughout Colombia.
Colombia’s revolution in Animal Welfare: An Exclusive Interview Is Colombia quietly becoming a global leader in animal welfare, surpassing even long-standing champions? Let’s find out.
Interviewer: Dr. Elena Ramirez,a leading expert in international animal welfare standards and policy,welcome to World-Today-News.com. Colombia’s recent strides in animal welfare are remarkable. Can you give our readers a broad overview of these advancements?
Dr. Ramirez: Thank you for having me. Yes, Colombia’s advancements are truly significant. The country is demonstrating a proactive and comprehensive approach to improving animal welfare across various sectors. This isn’t just about enacting new laws; it’s about creating a robust framework encompassing education, certification, and consistent enforcement.This holistic approach is what sets Colombia apart and positions it as a rising leader in animal welfare on the global stage. It’s a multifaceted strategy addressing not only the ethical treatment of animals but also the economic sustainability of related industries.
Interviewer: The article highlights several key resolutions. Can you delve deeper into their impact and importance? what makes these resolutions so effective?
Dr. Ramirez: Absolutely. Several key resolutions are instrumental in Colombia’s improved animal welfare standards. The Animal Welfare Conditions Manual (Resolution 253 of 2020) provides a foundational benchmark for assessing and improving conditions for various animals, including cattle, buffalo, poultry, and aquatic species. its detailed guidelines are crucial for creating a standardized approach to ethical animal husbandry. Then we have Resolution 000366 of 2024 , which directly addresses animal welfare in Zoocriaderos and animal exhibition events. Mandating basic animal welfare training for handlers is a critical element – ensuring that those who interact with animals daily understand appropriate handling techniques and recognize signs of distress or illness. Moreover, Resolution 00016409 of 2024 is groundbreaking in offering voluntary certification for livestock farms that meet high animal welfare standards based on Resolution 253 .This incentivizes farmers to prioritize animal welfare, recognizing the economic value of ethical practices. Resolution Mintransport and ICA 20223040006915 of 2022 establishes critical standards for the humane and safe transportation of animals – a frequently overlooked area in animal welfare but of paramount importance.
Interviewer: The voluntary certification program seems notably impactful in terms of positive reinforcement. Can you elaborate on how it works and its benefits?
Dr. Ramirez: The voluntary certification program, stemming from Resolution 00016409 of 2024 , offers a potent incentive for farms to improve their animal welfare practices. The program allows livestock producers to voluntarily seek certification based on meeting the standards laid out in Resolution 253 of 2020 . This creates a system of positive reinforcement, rewarding those who commit to ethical and responsible animal husbandry. Benefits extend beyond ethical considerations. Consumers increasingly favor products from farms with strong animal welfare credentials which boosts market appeal and profitability. Furthermore, this system of certification builds trust and transparency within the supply chain, strengthening consumer confidence in the origin and treatment of their food products.
Interviewer: What are some of the biggest challenges Colombia faces in continuing to improve its animal welfare standards?
Dr. Ramirez: Implementing lasting change requires addressing multiple hurdles. Effective enforcement of the existing resolutions and consistent monitoring of compliance are critical. additionally, providing extensive training and education for farmers and animal handlers necessitates resources and sustained commitment. Furthermore, engaging all stakeholders, including government agencies, industry representatives, and consumers, fosters collaboration needed for lasting success. Addressing these challenges ensures that these vital standards remain effective in promoting lasting benefits for animal welfare.
Interviewer: What recommendations would you give to other countries looking to improve their animal welfare legislation and programs?
Dr. Ramirez: I would highly recommend:
Developing a comprehensive national strategy: This should incorporate education,certification,and sustained enforcement mechanisms.
Establishing clear and measurable standards: This ensures transparency and accountability across all segments of the animal welfare sector.
Implementing a voluntary certification program: This rewards those who excel and encourages wider adoption of best practices.
Investing in education and training: Equipping those who work directly with animals with the knowledge and skills to provide ethical care is paramount.
* Fostering collaboration among stakeholders: Triumphant implementation requires a diverse coalition of government agencies, industry members, animal welfare organizations, and ethical consumers.
Interviewer: What does the future hold for Colombia’s efforts in animal welfare?
Dr. Ramirez: colombia’s commitment to animal welfare is undeniably strong. However, ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and adaptation will be essential for continued growth and progress. The recent milestones demonstrate a commitment to international standards and best practices, positioning Colombia as a role model for other nations striving to improve the lives of animals. The collaborative spirit shown across different stakeholder groups demonstrates a capacity for sustained and progressive change that is both encouraging and inspiring.
interviewer: Dr.Ramirez, thank you for sharing your expertise and providing such valuable insights.This conversation provides crucial context to help us understand the advancements in animal welfare that are taking place in Colombia.
